classification.difficultyReason: Combine daily capacity, a composite pentagonal cross-section and Pythagoras’ theorem to determine the prism’s length.

content.prompt: A farmer is making a trough that needs to be filled with water once each day. The trough is in the shape of a prism with pentagonal ends, as shown. The farmer has 60 horses that each drink about $10\text{ L}$ of water per day. Using the fact that $1\text{ cm}^3=1\text{ mL}$, what is the smallest length the trough needs to be to water the horses each day? Give your answer in centimetres, correct to two decimal places.

spec.description: Open pentagonal trough extending upwards to the right. The near end consists of a rectangle above a downward-pointing right-angled triangle. Both triangle sides retain their 40 cm labels, one with a curved leader. The upper vertical side is 30 cm. Ordinary source blue edges become black; the dashed cross-section divider retains semantic red.
spec.mathematics: The lower triangular cross-section has perpendicular sides of 40 cm. Its hypotenuse is the width of the rectangular portion, whose height is 30 cm. The longitudinal length is unspecified.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and the supplied right-angle mark are visible.

answer.short:
$\displaystyle\frac{1500}{2+3\sqrt2}\text{ cm}\approx240.28\text{ cm}$.

Find the pentagonal cross-sectional area, then divide the required volume by this area.
answer.worked:
The required daily capacity is
$$\begin{align*}V&=60\times10\\V&=600\text{ L}\\V&=600\,000\text{ cm}^3.\end{align*}$$
Let $w$ be the width of the rectangular portion. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}w^2&=40^2+40^2\\w^2&=3200\\w&=40\sqrt2\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
The pentagonal cross-section is a rectangle and a right-angled triangle:
$$\begin{align*}A&=30\times40\sqrt2+\frac12\times40\times40\\A&=1200\sqrt2+800\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
Using $V=A\ell$,
$$\begin{align*}\ell&=\frac{600\,000}{1200\sqrt2+800}\\\ell&=\frac{1500}{2+3\sqrt2}\text{ cm}\\\ell&\approx240.28\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
